## Goal

v11's Call 2 asks for **single counting**: the merged value of a cell should be the species'
suitability there, and extinction risk should enter once, as the weight at scoring. The v4 to v10
rule values a range cell `max(er_score, suitability)`, so the governing risk is baked into the
surface and multiplied in again at scoring. The new flag `SHARE_BASIS=cell` values a range cell by
its suitability alone wherever a suitability model covers it. That leaves one term open: **a range
cell no suitability model covers**. `RANGE_FILL` decides it:

- `er`: the cell is worth the governing `er_score` on the 0 to 100 scale (an MBTA bird: 10, an
  Endangered whale: 100). This is what the DPS rule has done since v9 and what the fold-in's
  density taxa inherited. Scoring multiplies by the same number again, so such a cell scores
  `er_score^2 / 100`.
- `presence`: the cell is worth 100, the range taken as presence. Scoring multiplies by the risk
  once.
- a **calibrated mean** (not built yet): the cell is worth what an average modelled cell of the
  species is worth, the mean of the suitability model over the cells it covers (for a density
  taxon, the survey's mean percentile value over its domain, after calibration). The unmodelled
  range then neither vanishes (er for a low-risk species) nor swamps the model (presence).

For a **range-only** species the fill is a constant over the whole range, so the share (value
divided by the species' own total) is the same under every fill. The fill matters for species
that have a model over part of their range: the density seabirds (survey domain vs the rest of
their BirdLife range), the DPS species (AquaMaps over part of the listed footprint), and any
range-and-AquaMaps taxon whose range extends beyond AquaMaps' cells.

This notebook reconstructs four species' merged surfaces from the committed merge input
(`mc_parts`) with the msens rules under each setting, maps them, and tabulates their global
totals and Program-Area shares. It changes nothing in the pipeline. The zone edits (occurrence
gate, encounter weight) are not applied here: they wrap every setting identically.

```{r}
#| label: setup

librarian::shelf(DBI, dplyr, duckdb, fs, ggplot2, glue, here, logger, readr, sf, tidyr, quiet = T)
source(here("libs/paths.R"))
dir_atlas <- glue("{dir_big_v}/marine-atlas")
dir_parts <- glue("{dir_atlas}/mc_parts")
merge_db  <- glue("{dir_atlas}/merge.duckdb")
stopifnot(dir_exists(dir_parts), file_exists(merge_db), file_exists(sdm_db))
g <- msens::grid_spec_for("global05")
con <- dbConnect(duckdb())
dbExecute(con, "SET threads = 4; SET memory_limit = '6GB'")
dbExecute(con, glue("SET temp_directory = '{dir_big}/derived/tmp_explore'"))
dbExecute(con, glue("ATTACH '{merge_db}' AS m (READ_ONLY)"))
dbExecute(con, glue("ATTACH '{sdm_db}' AS s (READ_ONLY)"))
dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE cell AS SELECT cell_id, lon, lat, area_km2, in_usa FROM s.cell")
dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE us_cells AS SELECT cell_id FROM cell WHERE in_usa")
dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE zone_pa AS SELECT z.val AS zone_key, zc.cell_id, zc.pct_covered
  FROM s.zone z JOIN s.zone_cell zc USING (zone_seq) WHERE z.fld = 'programarea_key'")
log_info("cells {dbGetQuery(con, 'SELECT count(*) n FROM cell')$n}; program-area cells {dbGetQuery(con, 'SELECT count(*) n FROM zone_pa')$n}")

# the four species: a density seabird, a listed fish with an FWS range and AquaMaps, an Arctic whale with an
# IUCN range and AquaMaps, and a DPS-listed pinniped (dps rule, AquaMaps over part of the footprint)
spp <- tribble(
  ~slug,        ~ms_merge_key,            ~zones,
  "shearwater", "ms_merge|BOTW:22698246", c("SOC", "CEC", "NOC"),
  "smelt",      "ms_merge|WORMS:282844",  c("CEC", "NOC"),
  "bowhead",    "ms_merge|WORMS:137086",  c("HOP", "CHU", "BFT"),
  "sealion",    "ms_merge|WORMS:254999",  c("COK", "GOA", "KOD", "SHU"))
spp <- spp |> inner_join(dbGetQuery(con, glue("SELECT mm.ms_merge_key, mm.mkey_id, t.er_score, t.scientific_name, t.common_name
  FROM m.mkey_map mm JOIN m.taxon t USING (ms_merge_key)
  WHERE mm.ms_merge_key IN ({paste(sprintf(\"'%s'\", spp$ms_merge_key), collapse = ',')})")), by = "ms_merge_key")
stopifnot(nrow(spp) == 4)
knitr::kable(spp |> select(slug, scientific_name, common_name, er_score, mkey_id))
```

## Reconstructing one species under each setting

```{r}
#| label: rules

suit_all <- c("am", "ax", "og", "gm", "nc", "cce")   # every suitability-type dataset the v11 merge knows
surfaces_of <- function(sp) {
  dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS b")
  dbExecute(con, glue("CREATE TABLE b AS SELECT ms_merge_key, ds_key, cell_id, val
    FROM read_parquet('{dir_parts}/mkey_id={sp$mkey_id}/*.parquet')"))
  ds <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT ds_key, count(*) n FROM b GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1")
  suit_ds <- intersect(suit_all, ds$ds_key)
  is_dens <- "dens_dom" %in% ds$ds_key
  is_dps  <- "dps_nmfs" %in% ds$ds_key
  # supersession as the merge applies it: a density survey replaces AquaMaps / AquaX inside its own domain
  if (is_dens) dbExecute(con, "DELETE FROM b WHERE ds_key IN ('am', 'ax') AND cell_id IN (SELECT cell_id FROM b WHERE ds_key = 'dens_dom')")
  dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS taxon; DROP TABLE IF EXISTS taxon_flags")
  dbExecute(con, glue("CREATE TABLE taxon AS SELECT '{sp$ms_merge_key}' AS ms_merge_key, {sp$er_score}::DOUBLE AS er_score"))
  dbExecute(con, glue("CREATE TABLE taxon_flags AS SELECT '{sp$ms_merge_key}' AS ms_merge_key,
    {length(suit_ds) > 0} AS has_suit, {any(!ds$ds_key %in% suit_all)} AS has_range"))
  out <- list()
  one <- function(sql) dbGetQuery(con, sql) |> select(cell_id, val) |> as_tibble()
  if (is_dps || is_dens) {
    # the cell-mode rules (dps_sql): no taxon basis exists for them; the baseline is today's er fill
    er_ds <- setdiff(ds$ds_key, suit_all); if (is_dps) er_ds <- "dps_nmfs"
    floor <- if (is_dens) sp$er_score else NULL
    for (fl in c("er", "presence")) {
      dbExecute(con, "DROP VIEW IF EXISTS dps_src"); dbExecute(con, "CREATE VIEW dps_src AS SELECT * FROM b WHERE ds_key NOT IN ('ch_nmfs', 'ch_fws', 'ca_nmfs')")
      out[[paste0("cell_", fl)]] <- one(msens::dps_sql(er_ds, suit_ds, src = "dps_src", er_floor = floor, fill = fl))
    }
    out$taxon <- NULL
  } else {
    msq <- msens::merge_sql(suit_ds, basis = "taxon")
    dbExecute(con, msq$b_range); dbExecute(con, msq$b_am_rng)
    out$taxon <- one(msq$global)
    for (fl in c("er", "presence")) out[[paste0("cell_", fl)]] <- one(msens::merge_sql(suit_ds, basis = "cell", fill = fl)$global)
  }
  # the calibrated-mean fill, derived: cells a suitability model covers keep their value; the rest take the
  # mean of those values (for a density taxon this is the survey's mean percentile over its domain)
  modelled <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("SELECT DISTINCT cell_id FROM b WHERE ds_key IN ({paste(sprintf(\"'%s'\", suit_ds), collapse = ',')})"))$cell_id
  base <- out$cell_er
  modelled <- intersect(modelled, base$cell_id)   # model cells INSIDE the footprint (beyond it they are masked away)
  m_val <- base |> filter(cell_id %in% modelled)
  fill_mean <- mean(m_val$val)
  out$cell_mean <- base |> mutate(val = if_else(cell_id %in% modelled, val, fill_mean))
  list(surfaces = out, ds = ds, suit_ds = suit_ds, rule = if (is_dps) "dps_sql (DPS-listed)" else if (is_dens) "dps_sql with er_floor (density taxon)" else "merge_sql",
       n_modelled = length(modelled), n_footprint = nrow(base), fill_mean = fill_mean)
}
```

```{r}
#| label: compute

res <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(spp))) {
  sp <- spp[i, ]; t0 <- Sys.time()
  res[[sp$slug]] <- surfaces_of(sp)
  log_info("{sp$slug}: rule {res[[sp$slug]]$rule}; footprint {res[[sp$slug]]$n_footprint} cells, {res[[sp$slug]]$n_modelled} modelled; mean modelled value {round(res[[sp$slug]]$fill_mean, 1)}; {round(as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = 'secs')))} s")
}
knitr::kable(bind_rows(lapply(names(res), \(k) tibble(
  species = k, rule = res[[k]]$rule, datasets = paste(res[[k]]$ds$ds_key, res[[k]]$ds$n, sep = ":", collapse = " "),
  footprint_cells = res[[k]]$n_footprint, modelled_cells = res[[k]]$n_modelled,
  unmodelled_share = round(1 - res[[k]]$n_modelled / res[[k]]$n_footprint, 3), mean_modelled_value = round(res[[k]]$fill_mean, 1)))),
  caption = "What each species' merge input holds, and how much of its footprint no suitability model covers (the cells the fill decides)")
```

## Global totals and Program-Area shares under each setting

The share of a zone is the species' value-weighted area inside it divided by the species'
global total (what `taxon_denom` and `share_run()` compute from the global surface, without the
zone edits). The composite's contribution is this share times the species' risk weight, so a
change in share is a proportional change in the species' contribution to every component score.

```{r}
#| label: shares

share_tab <- function(k) {
  r <- res[[k]]; sp <- spp[spp$slug == k, ]
  bind_rows(lapply(names(r$surfaces), \(s) {
    dbExecute(con, "DROP TABLE IF EXISTS surf"); duckdb_register(con, "surf_df", r$surfaces[[s]])
    dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE surf AS SELECT * FROM surf_df"); duckdb_unregister(con, "surf_df")
    tot <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT sum(v.val / 100.0 * c.area_km2) AS total, sum(CASE WHEN c.in_usa THEN v.val / 100.0 * c.area_km2 ELSE 0 END) AS total_usa
      FROM surf v JOIN cell c USING (cell_id)")
    z <- dbGetQuery(con, glue("SELECT z.zone_key, sum(v.val / 100.0 * c.area_km2 * z.pct_covered / 100.0) AS mass
      FROM surf v JOIN cell c USING (cell_id) JOIN zone_pa z USING (cell_id)
      WHERE z.zone_key IN ({paste(sprintf(\"'%s'\", sp$zones[[1]]), collapse = ',')}) GROUP BY 1"))
    tibble(species = k, setting = s, total_global = tot$total, total_usa = tot$total_usa) |>
      bind_cols(z |> mutate(share_pct = 100 * mass / tot$total) |> select(zone_key, share_pct) |> pivot_wider(names_from = zone_key, values_from = share_pct))
  }))
}
shares <- bind_rows(lapply(names(res), share_tab)) |>
  mutate(setting = factor(setting, c("taxon", "cell_er", "cell_presence", "cell_mean")), across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3))) |>
  arrange(species, setting)
write_csv(shares, here("data/explore/range_fill_shares.csv"))
knitr::kable(shares, caption = "Global value-weighted area (km2-equivalents), its US part, and the share (%) of the species' global total in the listed Program Areas, per setting. 'taxon' = the v4-v10 rule (max(er, suit) on range cells); the three 'cell' rows single-count on modelled cells and differ only in the unmodelled fill. Species on the DPS rule have no 'taxon' row: today's rule is cell_er.")
```

## Maps

Each panel is the merged value the species would carry under that setting, 0 to 100, on the
whole-range surface (what the Atlas would draw). Cells are averaged to 0.25 degree blocks for
species with large ranges. The outlined polygons are the Program Areas in the table.

```{r}
#| label: map-fun

ply <- tryCatch(st_read(glue("{dir_big}/derived/v2/ply_programareas_2026.gpkg"), quiet = TRUE), error = \(e) NULL)
shift360 <- function(x) ifelse(x < 0, x + 360, x)
map_species <- function(k) {
  r <- res[[k]]; sp <- spp[spp$slug == k, ]
  d <- bind_rows(lapply(names(r$surfaces), \(s) r$surfaces[[s]] |> mutate(setting = s)), .id = NULL) |>
    inner_join(dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT cell_id, lon, lat FROM cell") |> as_tibble(), by = "cell_id")
  big <- r$n_footprint > 150000
  pacific <- k %in% c("bowhead", "sealion")
  if (pacific) d$lon <- shift360(d$lon)
  if (big) d <- d |> mutate(lon = floor(lon * 4) / 4 + 0.125, lat = floor(lat * 4) / 4 + 0.125) |>
    group_by(setting, lon, lat) |> summarise(val = mean(val), .groups = "drop")
  lims <- d |> summarise(x0 = quantile(lon, 0.005), x1 = quantile(lon, 0.995), y0 = quantile(lat, 0.005), y1 = quantile(lat, 0.995))
  d$setting <- factor(d$setting, c("taxon", "cell_er", "cell_presence", "cell_mean"),
                      labels = c("taxon basis: max(er, suit)", "cell basis, er fill", "cell basis, presence fill", "cell basis, calibrated-mean fill"))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(lon, lat, fill = val)) + geom_raster() +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0, 100), name = "value") +
    coord_quickmap(xlim = c(lims$x0, lims$x1), ylim = c(lims$y0, lims$y1), expand = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~ setting, ncol = 2, drop = TRUE) + theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
    labs(title = glue("{sp$common_name} ({sp$scientific_name}), er_score {sp$er_score}\nrule: {r$rule}"),
         subtitle = glue("{format(r$n_footprint, big.mark = ',')} footprint cells, {format(r$n_modelled, big.mark = ',')} covered by a model; calibrated-mean fill = {round(r$fill_mean, 1)}"),
         x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  if (!is.null(ply)) {
    pz <- ply |> filter(programarea_key %in% sp$zones[[1]]) |> st_geometry()
    if (pacific) pz <- st_shift_longitude(pz)
    p <- p + geom_sf(data = st_sf(geometry = pz), inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, colour = "red", linewidth = 0.5) +
      coord_sf(xlim = c(lims$x0, lims$x1), ylim = c(lims$y0, lims$y1), expand = FALSE, default_crs = st_crs(4326))
  }
  p
}
```

#| fig-cap: "Black-vented shearwater: a Pacific density seabird (NCCOS survey inside its California Current domain, BirdLife range elsewhere). Under the er fill the unsurveyed range is worth 10; under presence 100; under the calibrated mean the survey's domain mean."
#| fig-width: 10

map_species("shearwater")

## Reading

```{r}
#| label: reading
#| output: asis

s <- shares |> group_by(species) |> summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~ NA)) |> select(species)
pick <- function(k, setting, col) shares |> filter(species == k, setting == !!setting) |> pull(all_of(col))
cat(glue("
- **Shearwater** (density seabird): the fill decides its California vs Alaska weight. Southern California share: er fill {round(pick('shearwater','cell_er','SOC'), 1)} %, presence {round(pick('shearwater','cell_presence','SOC'), 1)} %, calibrated mean {round(pick('shearwater','cell_mean','SOC'), 1)} %. Northern California: {round(pick('shearwater','cell_er','NOC'), 2)} / {round(pick('shearwater','cell_presence','NOC'), 2)} / {round(pick('shearwater','cell_mean','NOC'), 2)} %. (The Alaska bird changes come from wider-ranging density seabirds whose BirdLife range reaches Alaska; this one stops at British Columbia.)
- **Longfin smelt** (range + AquaMaps, er 100): the taxon basis gives Central California {round(pick('smelt','taxon','CEC'), 1)} % of the species; the cell basis {round(pick('smelt','cell_er','CEC'), 1)} % (er fill), {round(pick('smelt','cell_presence','CEC'), 1)} % (presence), {round(pick('smelt','cell_mean','CEC'), 1)} % (mean). Here the basis matters more than the fill.
- **Bowhead** (range + AquaMaps, er 100): Hope Basin {round(pick('bowhead','taxon','HOP'), 2)} % under the taxon basis vs {round(pick('bowhead','cell_er','HOP'), 2)} / {round(pick('bowhead','cell_presence','HOP'), 2)} / {round(pick('bowhead','cell_mean','HOP'), 2)} % under the cell basis with the three fills.
- **Steller sea lion** (dps rule): Cook Inlet {round(pick('sealion','cell_er','COK'), 2)} % (today's er fill), {round(pick('sealion','cell_presence','COK'), 2)} % (presence), {round(pick('sealion','cell_mean','COK'), 2)} % (mean).

"))
```

The table and maps say the same thing from two sides. The basis (max of risk and suitability vs
suitability alone) changes the **shape** of a high-risk species' surface wherever AquaMaps covers
its range. The fill changes the **balance** between the modelled and unmodelled parts of a
species' footprint, and that balance is only an issue for species modelled over part of their
range: the density seabirds above all, then the DPS species. For them `er` makes the unsurveyed
range nearly weightless for a low-risk species and dominant for a high-risk one (the fill tracks
the risk, which has nothing to do with how much of the species lives there), `presence` makes the
unsurveyed range outweigh the survey, and the calibrated mean treats an unsurveyed cell as an
average surveyed one, which is the only one of the three that does not depend on the risk score
or on an arbitrary ceiling. It is not yet a flag; this notebook derives it after the fact.
